nehemiah.name: Nehemiah, son of Hacaliah
nehemiah.role: King’s cup bearer who becomes governor of Judah
nehemiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
nehemiah.importance: Nehemiah weeps when he hears Jerusalem’s wall is broken. He asks the king to send him, and the wall is finished in fifty-two days. He makes the nobles give back fields taken for debt. Later he returns and throws Tobiah’s goods out of the temple. He shuts the gates on the Sabbath.
nehemiah.connections: He is the son of Hacaliah and brother of Hanani. He serves Artaxerxes. Sanballat and Tobiah oppose him.

hanani-nehemiah.name: Hanani, Nehemiah’s brother
hanani-nehemiah.role: Brother who brings the news about Jerusalem
hanani-nehemiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
hanani-nehemiah.importance: Hanani comes to Susa with men from Judah. They say the wall is broken and the gates are burned. Nehemiah weeps, fasts, and prays. After the wall is built, Nehemiah puts Hanani in charge of Jerusalem.
hanani-nehemiah.connections: Nehemiah calls him his brother. He shares charge of Jerusalem with Hananiah.

moses.name: Moses
moses.role: Earlier leader whose law the people read
moses.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
moses.importance: Moses does not act in this book. Nehemiah’s prayer repeats God’s word to him about scattering and gathering. Ezra reads his law to the people. They swear to walk in it.
moses.connections: The book calls him God’s servant. Ezra reads from the book of his law.

artaxerxes-ezra.name: Artaxerxes, the Persian king
artaxerxes-ezra.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
artaxerxes-ezra.importance: He sees that Nehemiah is sad and asks why. He agrees to send him to Judah. He gives letters and sends army captains and horsemen. In the king’s thirty-second year Nehemiah goes back to him.
artaxerxes-ezra.connections: Nehemiah is his cup bearer. The queen sits by him in chapter 2.

asaph-forest.name: Asaph, keeper of the king’s forest
asaph-forest.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
asaph-forest.importance: Nehemiah 2:8 is his only verse. The letter asks him for timber. The timber is for the gates, the city wall, and Nehemiah’s house. Asaph himself does not speak.
asaph-forest.connections: He keeps the forest for Artaxerxes. Nehemiah asks the king for a letter to him.

sanballat.name: Sanballat the Horonite
sanballat.role: Enemy who mocks and threatens the wall builders
sanballat.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
sanballat.importance: He is grieved when Nehemiah comes. He mocks the builders before the army of Samaria and plans an attack. He asks Nehemiah five times to meet him. Nehemiah will not come. In chapter 13 Nehemiah chases away his son-in-law.
sanballat.connections: He works with Tobiah and Geshem. A grandson of Eliashib the high priest is his son-in-law.

word.languageNote: This is the dictionary form of the name “Sanballat.”

tobiah-nehemiah.name: Tobiah the Ammonite
tobiah-nehemiah.role: Enemy with friends and family ties in Judah
tobiah-nehemiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
tobiah-nehemiah.importance: He says a fox could break the builders’ wall. He and Sanballat hire Shemaiah to scare Nehemiah. Nobles of Judah write to him, and he sends letters to frighten Nehemiah. Eliashib later gives him a temple room. Nehemiah throws his goods out.
tobiah-nehemiah.connections: He is the son-in-law of Shecaniah. His son Jehohanan marries the daughter of Meshullam.

word.languageNote: This is the dictionary form of the name “Tobiah.”

geshem.name: Geshem the Arabian
geshem.role: Enemy who asks Nehemiah to a meeting
geshem.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
geshem.importance: He joins Sanballat and Tobiah in mocking the builders. He and Sanballat ask Nehemiah to meet in the plain of Ono. Nehemiah says they mean to harm him and will not go. Sanballat’s letter says Gashmu reports that the Jews plan to rebel.
geshem.connections: He acts with Sanballat and Tobiah. Sanballat’s letter calls him Gashmu.

word.languageNote: This is the dictionary form of the name “Geshem.”

eliashib-nehemiah.name: Eliashib, the high priest
eliashib-nehemiah.role: High priest who builds the sheep gate
eliashib-nehemiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
eliashib-nehemiah.importance: Eliashib and his brother priests build the sheep gate and set up its doors. In chapter 13, Eliashib the priest makes a large temple room for Tobiah. Nehemiah calls this evil and empties the room. Nehemiah also chases away Eliashib’s grandson.
eliashib-nehemiah.connections: He is the father of Joiada. A son of Joiada is son-in-law to Sanballat.

wall-builders.name: The wall builders
wall-builders.role: Families, priests, and workers who repair the wall
wall-builders.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
wall-builders.importance: Each group repairs its own part, and many work across from their own houses. The nobles of Tekoa will not help. When enemies plan an attack, half hold spears while half work. Each builder wears his sword.
wall-builders.connections: They include priests, goldsmiths, rulers, and men from Jericho, Gibeon, and Mizpah.

shallum-daughters.name: Shallum and his daughters
shallum-daughters.role: Ruler and his daughters who repair the wall
shallum-daughters.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
shallum-daughters.importance: Nehemiah 3:12 is their only verse. Shallum and his daughters repair a part of the wall. They are the only women the repair list names as workers.
shallum-daughters.connections: Shallum is the son of Hallohesh. He rules half the district of Jerusalem.

meremoth.name: Meremoth, son of Uriah
meremoth.role: Man who repairs two parts of the wall
meremoth.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
meremoth.importance: He repairs a part of the wall near the fish gate. Later in the list he repairs a second part. It runs from the door of Eliashib’s house to the end of the house.
meremoth.connections: He is the son of Uriah, the son of Hakkoz.

meshullam-berechiah.name: Meshullam, son of Berechiah
meshullam-berechiah.role: Builder whose daughter marries Tobiah’s son
meshullam-berechiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
meshullam-berechiah.importance: He repairs two parts of the wall. One is across from his own room. Chapter 6 says his daughter married Tobiah’s son. That tie is one reason many in Judah were sworn to Tobiah.
meshullam-berechiah.connections: He is the son of Berechiah. His daughter is the wife of Jehohanan, Tobiah’s son.

nehemiah-azbuk.name: Nehemiah, son of Azbuk
nehemiah-azbuk.role: District ruler who repairs part of the wall
nehemiah-azbuk.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
nehemiah-azbuk.importance: Nehemiah 3:16 is his only verse. He repairs the wall across from the tombs of David and on to a pool. He is not Nehemiah the son of Hacaliah.
nehemiah-azbuk.connections: He is the son of Azbuk. He rules half the district of Beth Zur.

david.name: David
david.role: Earlier king named in places and in worship
david.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
david.importance: David does not act in this book. Builders repair the wall near his tombs and his city’s stairs. The Levites praise as he commanded. The singers carry his musical instruments at the wall.
david.connections: The book calls him the man of God. Solomon is his son.

debt-families.name: Families burdened by debt
debt-families.role: Parents and children short of food and land
debt-families.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
debt-families.importance: The people and their wives cry out. They have pledged fields, vineyards, and houses to buy grain and pay the king’s tribute. Some sons and daughters are now servants. Nehemiah is angry, and the nobles swear to give everything back.
debt-families.connections: They cry out against their brothers the Jews. The nobles and rulers are their lenders.

shemaiah-delaiah.name: Shemaiah, son of Delaiah
shemaiah-delaiah.role: Man who tells Nehemiah to hide in the temple
shemaiah-delaiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
shemaiah-delaiah.importance: Nehemiah visits his house. Shemaiah says men are coming to kill Nehemiah. He tells him to shut himself inside the temple. Nehemiah will not go in. He sees that God did not send Shemaiah.
shemaiah-delaiah.connections: He is the son of Delaiah. Nehemiah says Tobiah and Sanballat hired him.

noadiah-prophetess.name: Noadiah, the prophetess
noadiah-prophetess.role: Prophetess Nehemiah names in a prayer
noadiah-prophetess.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
noadiah-prophetess.importance: Nehemiah 6:14 is her only verse. Nehemiah asks God to remember her among those who tried to frighten him. The book gives none of her words.
noadiah-prophetess.connections: Nehemiah names her after Tobiah and Sanballat. He adds “the rest of the prophets.”

hananiah-fortress.name: Hananiah, commander of the fortress
hananiah-fortress.role: Governor of the fortress put over Jerusalem
hananiah-fortress.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
hananiah-fortress.importance: After the doors are set up, Nehemiah puts him in charge of Jerusalem with Hanani. Nehemiah calls him faithful and says he feared God above many. The two must keep the gates shut until the sun is hot.
hananiah-fortress.connections: Our reading text calls him the governor of the fortress. He shares charge of Jerusalem with Hanani.

zerubbabel.name: Zerubbabel
zerubbabel.role: Earlier leader named in the return lists
zerubbabel.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
zerubbabel.importance: Zerubbabel does not act in this book. His name stands first in the old list Nehemiah finds. Chapter 12 lists the priests and Levites who came up with him.
zerubbabel.connections: He is the son of Shealtiel. The lists name him with Jeshua.

jeshua-priest.name: Jeshua, son of Jozadak
jeshua-priest.role: Earlier priest named in the return lists
jeshua-priest.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jeshua-priest.importance: Jeshua does not act in this book. The old list names him right after Zerubbabel. Chapter 12 lists the chief priests of his days. It then follows his family down to Jaddua.
jeshua-priest.connections: He is the son of Jozadak and the father of Joiakim. Eliashib is his grandson.

nebuchadnezzar.name: Nebuchadnezzar
nebuchadnezzar.role: King of Babylon named in the return list
nebuchadnezzar.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
nebuchadnezzar.importance: Nehemiah 7:6 is his only verse. He does not act in this book. The list counts the people who came back from where he carried them.
nebuchadnezzar.connections: He is king of Babylon. The list says he carried the people away.

returning-families.name: The returning families and temple workers
returning-families.role: Families and temple workers in the earlier return list
returning-families.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
returning-families.importance: Jerusalem is large, but few people live in it. Nehemiah plans to count the people and finds this older list. It counts 42,360 people by family and town. Some priests could not find their records and were kept from serving.
returning-families.connections: They came up with Zerubbabel and Jeshua. Nehemiah finds their list.

asaph-singer.name: Asaph, the singer
asaph-singer.role: Earlier singer whose sons sing at the temple
asaph-singer.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
asaph-singer.importance: Asaph does not act in this book. The return list counts 148 singers from his family. His sons lead the thanksgiving and blow trumpets at the wall. Chapter 12 looks back to the days of David and Asaph.
asaph-singer.connections: Mattaniah, Uzzi, and Zechariah are named among his sons.

ezra.name: Ezra
ezra.role: Priest and scribe who reads God’s law
ezra.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ezra.importance: Ezra stands on a wooden pulpit and reads the law from early morning until midday. The people weep, and he and the leaders tell them not to mourn. The next day they study the law and keep the feast of booths. At the wall, Ezra the scribe walks before one company.
ezra.connections: The people ask him to bring the book. Nehemiah the governor and the Levites stand with him.

law-teachers.name: The teachers of God’s law
law-teachers.role: Levites who help the people understand the reading
law-teachers.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
law-teachers.importance: They read the law clearly and give the sense. The people understand and weep. The Levites calm them and say the day is holy. In chapter 9, Levites stand on the stairs and lead the long prayer.
law-teachers.connections: Chapter 8 names thirteen of them, with Jeshua first. They work beside Ezra and Nehemiah.

sherebiah.name: Sherebiah
sherebiah.role: Levite who explains the law and leads the prayer
sherebiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
sherebiah.importance: He is one of the Levites who help the people understand Ezra’s reading. In chapter 9 he stands on the stairs and cries out to the LORD. He helps call the people to stand and bless God. His name is on the sealed covenant.
sherebiah.connections: He is listed among the Levites with Jeshua, Bani, and Kadmiel.

shabbethai-nehemiah.name: Shabbethai, the Levite in Nehemiah
shabbethai-nehemiah.role: Levite who teaches and has charge of outside work
shabbethai-nehemiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
shabbethai-nehemiah.importance: In chapter 8 a Levite named Shabbethai helps the people understand the law. In chapter 11 Shabbethai and Jozabad are chiefs of the Levites. They have charge of the outside business of God’s house.
shabbethai-nehemiah.connections: Chapter 8 lists him among the teaching Levites. Chapter 11 names him with Jozabad.

joshua.name: Joshua
joshua.role: Earlier leader named at the feast of booths
joshua.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
joshua.importance: Nehemiah 8:17 is his only verse. The people build shelters and live in them for the feast. The verse says Israel had not done so since his days.
joshua.connections: The book calls him the son of Nun.

abraham.name: Abraham
abraham.role: Father of the people, named in the prayer
abraham.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
abraham.importance: Abraham does not act in this book. The prayer says God brought him out of Ur of the Chaldees. God found his heart faithful and promised the land to his offspring. The prayer says God kept that word.
abraham.connections: The prayer says God chose Abram and named him Abraham.

sihon.name: Sihon
sihon.role: Earlier king whose land Israel took
sihon.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
sihon.importance: Nehemiah 9:22 is his only verse. The prayer says God gave Israel kingdoms and peoples. Israel took the land of Sihon, the land of the king of Heshbon.
sihon.connections: The prayer names him with Og king of Bashan.

og.name: Og
og.role: Earlier king of Bashan whose land Israel took
og.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
og.importance: Nehemiah 9:22 is his only verse. The prayer says God gave Israel kingdoms and peoples. Israel took the land of Og king of Bashan.
og.connections: The prayer names him right after Sihon.

covenant-families.name: The families making the covenant
covenant-families.role: Men, women, and children who swear to keep God’s law
covenant-families.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
covenant-families.importance: They take an oath to walk in God’s law. They promise not to marry their children to the peoples of the land. They will not buy on the Sabbath. They will bring wood, first fruits, and tithes to God’s house.
covenant-families.connections: They join their brothers the nobles, who sealed the written covenant.

jeshua-azaniah.name: Jeshua, son of Azaniah
jeshua-azaniah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jeshua-azaniah.importance: Nehemiah 10:9 names him first among the Levites who sealed the covenant. The verse says nothing more about him.
jeshua-azaniah.connections: He is the son of Azaniah. He is not the priest Jeshua, the son of Jozadak.

aaron.name: Aaron
aaron.role: Earlier priest whose sons serve at the temple
aaron.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
aaron.importance: Aaron does not act in this book. The covenant says a priest of his line must be present when Levites take tithes. In chapter 12 the Levites set apart a share for his sons.
aaron.connections: The priests are called his sons or descendants.

levi.name: Levi
levi.role: Father of the Levites, named in the covenant
levi.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
levi.importance: Levi does not act in this book. The covenant says the children of Levi will bring grain, new wine, and oil. They bring them to the temple rooms.
levi.connections: The Levites are called his children.

city-settlers.name: The families settling in Jerusalem
city-settlers.role: Households chosen or willing to live in Jerusalem
city-settlers.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
city-settlers.importance: The princes already live in Jerusalem. The rest cast lots, and one family in ten moves into the city. The people bless the men who offer to go. The city had been large with few people in it.
city-settlers.connections: They come from Judah and Benjamin, with priests, Levites, and gatekeepers.

solomon.name: Solomon
solomon.role: Earlier king named in worship rules and a warning
solomon.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
solomon.importance: Solomon does not act in this book. The singers and gatekeepers serve as David and Solomon commanded. In chapter 13 Nehemiah says foreign women caused even Solomon to sin. He uses this to warn men who married foreign women.
solomon.connections: He is David’s son and king of Israel.

wall-singers.name: The singers at the wall’s dedication
wall-singers.role: Two companies who give thanks on the wall
wall-singers.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
wall-singers.importance: The singers gather from the villages around Jerusalem. Nehemiah sets two companies on the wall, and they walk in opposite directions. They meet and stand in God’s house. The joy of Jerusalem is heard far away.
wall-singers.connections: Ezra the scribe goes before one company. Nehemiah follows the other.

balaam.name: Balaam
balaam.role: Earlier man hired to curse Israel
balaam.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
balaam.importance: Nehemiah 13:2 is his only verse. The people read that he was hired to curse Israel. God turned the curse into a blessing. After hearing this, they separate the mixed crowd from Israel.
balaam.connections: The Ammonites and Moabites hired him against Israel.

foreign-families-nehemiah.name: The foreign wives and their children in Nehemiah
foreign-families-nehemiah.role: Wives and children from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab
foreign-families-nehemiah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
foreign-families-nehemiah.importance: Nehemiah sees Jews who married women of Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab. Half their children cannot speak the Jews’ language. He curses the men, strikes some, and makes them swear. The book gives none of the wives’ or children’s words.
foreign-families-nehemiah.connections: They are the wives and children of Jews. None of them is named.
